title: What If an Asteroid Was Spotted Just 19 Hours Before It Hit? In 2008 One Was

scenes.text: What if we spotted an asteroid just 19 hours before it hit Earth? In 2008, we did.
On October 6, a telescope in Arizona picked up a faint moving dot. The first orbit said: impact tomorrow.
Astronomers tracked it through the night and worked out where it would strike: the desert of northern Sudan.
It arrived on schedule, at more than 12 kilometers a second: a rock the size of a car, weighing about 80 tons.
It exploded 37 kilometers up, over empty desert.
Two months later, students from Khartoum walked the sand in a line and picked up dozens of black stones: pieces of an asteroid people had watched arrive.

description:
What if an asteroid was discovered only 19 hours before it hit Earth?
It happened. On 6 October 2008 the Catalina Sky Survey telescope on Mount Lemmon, Arizona, found a small object, later named 2008 TC3, and the first orbit calculations showed it would strike Earth the next day. Observers tracked it through its last hours, and the predicted impact point in the Nubian Desert of northern Sudan was correct. The asteroid was about 4 metres across and weighed roughly 80 tonnes; it entered the atmosphere at about 12.4 km per second on 7 October and exploded 37 km up. In December 2008, Peter Jenniskens, Muawia Shaddad and staff and students of the University of Khartoum searched the desert and recovered 47 meteorites weighing 3.95 kg, named Almahata Sitta ('Station Six') after a nearby railway stop.
What should we run through next?
first_comment: This rock was only about four metres wide, so it burst high in the air. How much warning would you want for a big one?
